She was asked, “Why do you go out when you know that ‘Umar dislikes that and is jealous?” She said, “What prevents him from forbidding me?” He said, “What prevents him is the saying of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: ‘Do not prevent Allah’s female servants from Allah’s mosques.’”

Ibn ‘Abbas said to his caller to prayer on a rainy day, “When you say, ‘I testify that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah,’ do not say, ‘Come to prayer.’ Say, ‘Pray in your homes.’” It was as though the people disapproved. He said, “Someone better than me did this. Friday prayer is an obligation, but I disliked putting you in difficulty, so that you would walk through mud and slippery ground.”

english_blocks: Ahmad related to us. He said: ‘Abdullah ibn Wahb related to us. She said: People used to come on Friday from their homes and from al-‘Awali. They would come through the dust; dust and sweat would affect them, and sweat would come out of them. One of them came to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, while he was with me. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “If only you would purify yourselves for this day of yours.”

english_blocks: Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr al-Muqaddami related to us. He said: Harami ibn ‘Umarah related to us. He said: Abu Khaldah—he is Khalid ibn Dinar—related to us. He said: I heard Anas ibn Malik say:

arabic_blocks: [875] حدثنا قتيبة بن سعيد قال: حدثنا يعقوب بن عبد الرحمن بن محمد بن عبد الله بن عبد القاري القرشي الإسكندراني قال: حدثنا أبو حازم بن دينار أن رجالا أتوا سهل بن سعد الساعدي وقد امتروا في المنبر مم عوده فسألوه عن ذلك، فقال والله إني لأعرف مما هو ولقد رأيته أول يوم وضع وأول يوم جلس عليه رسول الله ﷺ أرسل رسول الله ﷺ إلى فلانة امرأة قد سماها سهل مري غلامك النجار أن يعمل لي أعوادا أجلس عليهن إذا كلمت الناس فأمرته فعملها من طرفاء الغابة ثم جاء بها فأرسلت إلى رسول الله ﷺ فأمر بها فوضعت ها هنا ثم رأيت رسول الله ﷺ صلى عليها وكبر وهو عليها ثم ركع وهو عليها ثم نزل القهقري فسجد في أصل المنبر ثم عاد فلما فرغ أقبل على الناس، فقال أيها الناس إنما صنعت هذا لتأتموا ولتعلموا صلاتي

Some men came to Sahl ibn Sa‘d al-Sa‘idi, having disagreed about what wood the pulpit was made of. They asked him about it. He said, “By Allah, I certainly know what it is made of. I saw it on the first day it was put in place and the first day the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sat on it. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sent to a certain woman, whom Sahl named: ‘Instruct your slave, the carpenter, to make me pieces of wood on which I can sit when I speak to the people.’ She instructed him, and he made them from tamarisk from al-Ghabah. Then he brought them, and she sent them to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He ordered them to be put here. Then I saw the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, pray on them and say the takbir while on them, then bow while on them. Then he descended backwards and prostrated at the foot of the pulpit, then returned. When he finished, he turned to the people and said, ‘People, I only did this so that you would follow me and learn my prayer.’”

english_blocks: And Mahmud said: Abu Usamah related to us. He said: Hisham ibn ‘Urwah related to us. He said: Fatimah bint al-Mundhir informed me, from Asma’ bint Abi Bakr:

She said: I went in to ‘A’ishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, while the people were praying. I said, ‘What is happening with the people?’ She pointed her head towards the sky. I said, ‘A sign?’ She nodded her head, meaning yes. She said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prolonged it greatly, until faintness overcame me. Beside me was a waterskin containing water, so I opened it and began pouring from it over my head. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, finished, and the sun had cleared. He addressed the people and praised Allah as He deserves, then said, ‘Now then.’ And she said: Some women of the Ansar made a noise, so I turned towards them to quiet them. I said to ‘A’ishah, ‘What did he say?’ She said: He said, ‘There is nothing that I had not been shown before that I have not seen at this place where I stand, even the Garden and the Fire. It has been revealed to me that you will be tried in the graves with a trial like, or close to, the trial of the false messiah. One of you will be approached and asked, “What do you know of this man?” As for the believer—or he said, the one who is certain; Hisham was unsure—he will say, “He is the Messenger of Allah. He is Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He brought us clear proofs and guidance, so we believed, responded, followed and affirmed the truth.” He will be told, “Sleep, righteous one. We already knew that you did indeed believe in him.” As for the hypocrite—or he said, the doubter; Hisham was unsure—he will be asked, “What do you know of this man?” He will say, “I do not know. I heard people saying something, so I said it.”’
Hisham said: Fatimah did indeed tell it to me, and I retained it, except that she mentioned what would be made severe for him.

arabic_blocks: [881] حدثنا محمد بن معمر قال: حدثنا أبو عاصم عن جرير بن حازم قال: سمعت الحسن يقول: حدثنا عمرو بن تغلب أن رسول الله ﷺ أتى بمال أو بسبي فقسمه فأعطى رجالا وترك رجالا فبلغه أن الذين ترك عتبوا فحمد الله ثم أثنى عليه، ثم قال: أما بعد فوالله إني لأعطي الرجل وأدع الرجل والذي أدع أحب إلي من الذي أعطى ولكن أعطي أقواما لما أرى في قلوبهم من الجزع والهلع وأكل أقواما إلى ما جعل الله في قلوبهم من الغنى والخير فيهم عمرو بن تغلب فوالله ما أحب أن لي بكلمة رسول الله ﷺ حمر النعم تابعه يونس
english_blocks: Muhammad ibn Ma‘mar related to us. He said: Abu ‘Asim related to us, from Jarir ibn Hazim. He said: I heard al-Hasan saying: ‘Amr ibn Taghlib related to us:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was brought wealth or captives. He divided it, giving to some men and leaving others. News reached him that those he had left were displeased. He praised Allah, then extolled Him, then said, ‘Now then. By Allah, I give to one man and leave another, although the one I leave is more beloved to me than the one I give to. But I give to some people because of the distress and anxiety I see in their hearts, and I entrust others to the contentment and goodness that Allah has placed in their hearts. Among them is ‘Amr ibn Taghlib.’ By Allah, I would not wish to have red camels in exchange for those words of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.
Yunus corroborated this.

arabic_blocks: [882] حدثنا يحيى بن بكير قال: حدثنا الليث عن عقيل عن ابن شهاب قال: أخبرني عروة أن عائشة أخبرته أن رسول الله ﷺ خرج ذات ليلة من جوف الليل فصلى في المسجد فصلى رجال بصلاته فأصبح الناس فتحدثوا فاجتمع أكثر منهم فصلوا معه فأصبح الناس فتحدثوا فكثر أهل المسجد من الليلة الثالثة فخرج رسول الله ﷺ فصلوا بصلاته فلما كانت الليلة الرابعة عجز المسجد عن أهله حتى خرج لصلاة الصبح فلما قضى الفجر أقبل على الناس فتشهد، ثم قال: أما بعد فإنه لم يخف علي مكانكم لكني خشيت أن تفرض عليكم فتعجزوا عنها تابعه يونس
english_blocks: Yahya ibn Bukayr related to us. He said: Al-Layth related to us, from ‘Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab. He said: ‘Urwah informed me that ‘A’ishah informed him:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went out one night in the middle of the night and prayed in the mosque. Some men prayed following his prayer. In the morning, the people spoke about it, and more of them gathered and prayed with him. In the morning, the people spoke about it, and the number of people in the mosque increased on the third night. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came out, and they prayed following his prayer. On the fourth night, the mosque could not hold its people, until he came out for the dawn prayer. When he had finished the dawn prayer, he faced the people and pronounced the testimony of faith, then said, ‘Now then. Your presence was not hidden from me, but I feared that it would be made obligatory upon you and you would be unable to perform it.’
Yunus corroborated this.

english_blocks: Isma‘il ibn Aban related to us. He said: Ibn al-Ghasil related to us. He said: ‘Ikrimah related to us, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both:

He said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, ascended the pulpit. It was the last gathering in which he sat. He had wrapped a cloak around his shoulders and tied a dark headcloth around his head. He praised Allah and extolled Him, then said, ‘People, come to me.’ They gathered towards him. Whoever takes charge of any part of the community of Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and is able in that position to harm someone or benefit someone, should accept from those among them who do good and pardon those among them who do wrong.’

arabic_blocks: [891] حدثنا إبراهيم بن المنذر قال: حدثنا الوليد قال: حدثنا أبو عمرو قال: حدثني إسحاق بن عبد الله بن أبي طلحة عن أنس بن مالك قال أصابت الناس سنة على عهد النبي ﷺ فبينا النبي ﷺ يخطب في يوم جمعة قام أعرابي، فقال: يا رسول الله هلك المال وجاع العيال فادع الله لنا فرفع يديه وما نرى في السماء قزعة فوالذي نفسي بيده ما وضعها حتى ثار السحاب أمثال الجبال ثم لم ينزل عن منبره حتى رأيت المطر يتحادر على لحيته ﷺ فمطرنا يومنا ذلك ومن الغد وبعد الغد والذي يليه حتى الجمعة الأخرى وقام ذلك الأعرابي أو قال غيره، فقال: يا رسول الله تهدم البناء وغرق المال فادع الله لنا فرفع يديه، فقال اللهم حوالينا ولا علينا فما يشير بيده إلى ناحية من السحاب إلا انفرجت وصارت المدينة مثل الجوبة وسال الوادي قناة شهرا ولم يجئ أحد من ناحية إلا حدث بالجود
english_blocks: Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir related to us. He said: Al-Walid related to us. He said: Abu ‘Amr related to us. He said: Ishaq ibn ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Talhah related to me, from Anas ibn Malik:

He said: The people suffered a drought in the time of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. While the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was delivering the sermon one Friday, a Bedouin stood up and said, ‘Messenger of Allah, the livestock have perished and the dependants are hungry. Supplicate to Allah for us.’ He raised his hands, and we could see no patch of cloud in the sky. By Him in whose hand is my soul, he had not lowered them before clouds rose like mountains. Then he had not come down from his pulpit before I saw rain streaming down his beard, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Rain fell upon us that day, the next day, the day after it and the day following, until the next Friday. That Bedouin—or he said, someone else—stood up and said, ‘Messenger of Allah, the buildings have collapsed and the livestock have drowned. Supplicate to Allah for us.’ He raised his hands and said, ‘Allah, around us and not upon us.’ Whenever he pointed his hand towards a part of the clouds, they parted. Madinah became like an opening, and the valley of Qanat flowed for a month. No one came from any direction without speaking of the abundant rain.

english_blocks: Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri.

I went on an expedition with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, towards Najd. We faced the enemy and formed ranks opposite them. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood to lead us in prayer. One group stood with him, praying, while another group faced the enemy. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, bowed with those who were with him and made two prostrations. Then they went to take the place of the group that had not prayed. That group came, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed one unit with them and made two prostrations. Then he gave the closing greeting. Each of them then stood and prayed one unit for himself and made two prostrations.

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood, and the people stood with him. He said ‘Allah is greatest,’ and they said it with him. He bowed, and some of the people bowed. Then he prostrated, and they prostrated with him. Then he stood for the second unit. Those who had prostrated stood and guarded their brothers. The other group came and bowed and prostrated with him. All the people were in prayer, but they were guarding one another.

english_blocks: Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri. He said: Salim ibn ‘Abdullah informed me that ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar said:

‘Umar took a robe of thick silk that was being sold in the market. He took it and came to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and said, ‘Messenger of Allah, buy this and adorn yourself with it for Eid and for delegations.’ The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to him, ‘This is only the clothing of one who has no share.’ ‘Umar remained as long as Allah willed him to remain. Then the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sent him a robe of silk brocade. ‘Umar came with it and brought it to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He said, ‘Messenger of Allah, you said, “This is only the clothing of one who has no share,” yet you have sent me this robe.’ The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to him, ‘Sell it, or meet your need with it.’

english_blocks: Ahmad related to us. He said: Ibn Wahb related to us. He said: ‘Amr informed us that Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman al-Asadi related to him, from ‘Urwah, from ‘A’ishah. She said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came in to me while two girls were with me, singing the songs of Bu‘ath. He lay down on the bed and turned his face away. Abu Bakr came in and rebuked me, saying, ‘A pipe of Satan in the presence of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace!’ The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, turned towards him and said, ‘Leave them both.’ When he became inattentive, I signalled to the two of them, and they went out.

It was an Eid day, and the Black people were playing with shields and spears. Either I asked the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, or he said, ‘Would you like to watch?’ I said, ‘Yes.’ He stood me behind him, my cheek against his cheek, while he was saying, ‘Carry on, Banu Arfidah!’ When I grew tired, he said, ‘Is that enough for you?’ I said, ‘Yes.’ He said, ‘Then go.’

english_blocks: Musaddad related to us. He said: Isma‘il related to us, from Ayyub, from Muhammad, from Anas. He said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘Whoever slaughtered before the prayer must do it again.’ A man stood and said, ‘This is a day on which meat is desired,’ and he mentioned some of his neighbours. It was as though the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, accepted his statement. He said, ‘I have a young she-goat dearer to me than two sheep for meat.’ The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, allowed it for him.
I do not know whether the permission extended to anyone other than him or not.

english_blocks: ‘Uthman related to us. He said: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from al-Sha‘bi, from al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both. He said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, addressed us on the day of Adha after the prayer. He said, ‘Whoever prays our prayer and performs our sacrifice has fulfilled the sacrifice. Whoever sacrifices before the prayer has done so before the prayer, and has no sacrifice.’ Abu Burdah ibn Niyar, al-Bara’s maternal uncle, said, ‘Messenger of Allah, I sacrificed my sheep before the prayer. I knew that today was a day of eating and drinking, and I wanted my sheep to be the first thing slaughtered in my house. So I slaughtered my sheep and ate my midday meal before coming to the prayer.’ He said, ‘Your sheep is a sheep for meat.’ He said, ‘Messenger of Allah, we have a young she-goat that is dearer to me than two sheep. Will it suffice for me?’ He said, ‘Yes, but it will not suffice for anyone after you.’

arabic_blocks: [913] حدثنا سعيد بن أبي مريم قال: حدثنا محمد بن جعفر قال: أخبرني زيد عن عياض بن عبد الله بن أبي سرح عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال: كان رسول الله ﷺ يخرج يوم الفطر والأضحى إلى المصلى فأول شيء يبدأ به الصلاة ثم ينصرف فيقوم مقابل الناس والناس جلوس على صفوفهم فيعظهم ويوصيهم ويأمرهم فإن كان يريد أن يقطع بعثا قطعه أو يأمر بشيء أمر به ثم ينصرف قال أبو سعيد فلم يزل الناس على ذلك حتى خرجت مع مروان وهو أمير المدينة في أضحى أو فطر فلما أتينا المصلى إذا منبر بناه كثير بن الصلت فإذا مروان يريد أن يرتقيه قبل أن يصلي فجبذت بثوبه فجبذني فارتفع فخطب قبل الصلاة فقلت له غيرتم والله، فقال أبا سعيد قد ذهب ما تعلم فقلت: ما أعلم والله خير مما لا أعلم، فقال إن الناس لم يكونوا يجلسون لنا بعد الصلاة فجعلتها قبل الصلاة
english_blocks: Sa‘id ibn Abi Maryam related to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ja‘far related to us. He said: Zayd informed me, from ‘Iyad ibn ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Sarh, from Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri. He said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would go out on the day of Fitr and Adha to the prayer ground. The first thing he began with was the prayer. Then he would turn and stand facing the people, while they remained seated in their rows. He would admonish them, counsel them and give them instructions. If he wished to dispatch a force, he dispatched it, or to order something, he ordered it. Then he would leave.

Abu Sa‘id said: The people continued in this way until I went out with Marwan, who was the governor of Madinah, on Adha or Fitr. When we reached the prayer ground, there was a pulpit built by Kathir ibn al-Salt. Marwan wanted to climb it before praying. I pulled at his garment, and he pulled me. He went up and delivered the sermon before the prayer. I said to him, ‘By Allah, you have changed things.’ He said, ‘Abu Sa‘id, what you know has gone.’ I said, ‘By Allah, what I know is better than what I do not know.’ He said, ‘The people would not remain seated for us after the prayer, so I placed it before the prayer.’

english_blocks: Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya related to us, from Sufyan. He said: ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Abis related to me. He said: I heard Ibn ‘Abbas:

He was asked, ‘Did you attend Eid with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace?’ He said, ‘Yes. Had it not been for my young age, I would not have attended it. He reached the marker by the house of Kathir ibn al-Salt, prayed, then delivered a sermon. Then he went to the women with Bilal. He admonished them, reminded them and commanded them to give charity. I saw them reaching with their hands and throwing it into Bilal’s garment. Then he and Bilal went to his house.’

arabic_blocks: [935] حدثني إسحاق بن إبراهيم بن نصر قال: حدثنا عبد الرزاق قال: حدثنا ابن جريج قال: أخبرني عطاء عن جابر بن عبد الله قال: سمعته يقول قام النبي ﷺ يوم الفطر فصلى فبدأ بالصلاة ثم خطب فلما فرغ نزل فأتى النساء فذكرهن وهو يتوكأ على يد بلال وبلال باسط ثوبه يلقي فيه النساء الصدقة قلت لعطاء زكاة يوم الفطر قال لا ولكن صدقة يتصدقن حينئذ تلقي فتخها ويلقين قلت: أترى حقا على الإمام ذلك يأتيهن ويذكرهن قال إنه لحق عليهم وما لهم لا يفعلونه
english_blocks: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Nasr related to me. He said: ‘Abd al-Razzaq related to us. He said: Ibn Jurayj related to us. He said: ‘Ata’ informed me, from Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah. He said: I heard him say:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood on the day of Fitr and prayed. He began with prayer, then delivered a sermon. When he finished, he came down and went to the women and reminded them, leaning on Bilal’s hand. Bilal had spread out his garment, into which the women were throwing charity.

I said to ‘Ata’, ‘The zakat of the day of Fitr?’ He said, ‘No, but charity they were giving at that time. A woman would throw in her large rings, and they would throw things in.’ I said, ‘Do you consider that a duty upon the imam—to go to them and remind them?’ He said, ‘It is certainly a duty upon them. Why do they not do it?’

arabic_blocks: [936] قال ابن جريج وأخبرني الحسن بن مسلم عن طاوس عن ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما قال شهدت الفطر مع النبي ﷺ وأبي بكر وعمر وعثمان رضى الله تعالى عنهم يصلونها قبل الخطبة ثم يخطب بعد خرج النبي ﷺ كأني أنظر إليه حين يجلس بيده ثم أقبل يشقهم حتى جاء النساء معه بلال، فقال { يا أيها النبي إذا جاءك المؤمنات يبايعنك } الآية، ثم قال حين فرغ منها آنتن على ذلك قالت امرأة واحدة منهن لم يجبه غيرها نعم لا يدري حسن من هي قال: فتصدقن فبسط بلال ثوبه، ثم قال هلم لكن فداء أبي وأمي فيلقين الفتخ والخواتيم في ثوب بلال قال عبد الرزاق الفتخ الخواتيم العظام كانت في الجاهلية
english_blocks: Ibn Jurayj said: Al-Hasan ibn Muslim also informed me, from Tawus, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both. He said:

I attended Fitr with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and Abu Bakr, ‘Umar and ‘Uthman, may Allah Most High be pleased with them. They would pray it before the sermon, then he would deliver the sermon afterwards. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went out. It is as though I am looking at him as he motions with his hand for people to sit. Then he went forward, making his way through them, until he came to the women with Bilal. He said, ‘O Prophet, when believing women come to you pledging allegiance to you’—the verse. When he finished it, he said, ‘Are you committed to that?’ One woman among them said, ‘Yes’; no one else answered him.
Hasan did not know who she was.
He said, ‘Then give charity.’ Bilal spread out his garment, then said, ‘Come, may my father and mother be ransomed for you.’ They began throwing large rings and rings into Bilal’s garment.
‘Abd al-Razzaq said: The fatakh were the large rings that were used in the time of ignorance.

arabic_blocks: [937] حدثنا أبو معمر قال: حدثنا عبد الوارث قال: حدثنا أيوب عن حفصة بنت سيرين قالت كنا نمنع جوارينا أن يخرجن يوم العيد فجاءت امرأة فنزلت قصر بني خلف فأتيتها فحدثت أن زوج أختها غزا مع النبي ﷺ اثنتي عشرة غزوة فكانت أختها معه في ست غزوات فقالت فكنا نقوم على المرضى ونداوي الكلمى فقالت: يا رسول الله على إحدانا بأس إذا لم يكن لها جلباب أن لا تخرج، فقال لتلبسها صاحبتها من جلبابها فليشهدن الخير ودعوة المؤمنين قالت حفصة فلما قدمت أم عطية أتيتها فسألتها أسمعت في كذا وكذا قالت نعم بأبي وقلما ذكرت النبي ﷺ إلا قالت بأبي قال ليخرج العواتق ذوات الخدور أو قال العواتق وذوات الخدور شك أيوب والحيض ويعتزل الحيض المصلي وليشهدن الخير ودعوة المؤمنين قالت فقلت لها آلحيض قالت نعم أليس الحائض تشهد عرفات وتشهد كذا وتشهد كذا
english_blocks: Abu Ma‘mar related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Warith related to us. He said: Ayyub related to us, from Hafsah bint Sirin. She said:

We used to prevent our girls from going out on the day of Eid. A woman came and stayed at the palace of Banu Khalaf. I went to her, and she related that her sister’s husband had gone on twelve expeditions with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and her sister was with him on six expeditions. She said, ‘We used to tend the sick and treat the wounded.’ She said, ‘Messenger of Allah, is there any blame on one of us if she has no outer garment and does not go out?’ He said, ‘Let her companion cover her with her outer garment, and let them witness the good and the supplication of the believers.’ Hafsah said: When Umm ‘Atiyyah arrived, I went to her and asked her, ‘Did you hear about such-and-such?’ She said, ‘Yes, may my father be ransomed for him.’
She seldom mentioned the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, without saying, ‘May my father be ransomed for him.’
He said, ‘Let the young women in seclusion go out’—or he said, ‘The young women and the women in seclusion’—
Ayyub was uncertain.

‘And the menstruating women. Let the menstruating women keep apart from the prayer ground, and let them witness the good and the supplication of the believers.’ She said: I said to her, ‘The menstruating women?’ She said, ‘Yes. Does not a menstruating woman attend ‘Arafat, and attend such-and-such, and attend such-and-such?’

english_blocks: Musaddad related to us. He said: Abu al-Ahwas related to us. He said: Mansur ibn al-Mu‘tamir related to us, from al-Sha‘bi, from al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib. He said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, addressed us on the Day of Sacrifice after the prayer. He said, ‘Whoever prays our prayer and performs our sacrifice has fulfilled the sacrifice. Whoever sacrifices before the prayer, that is a sheep for meat.’ Abu Burdah ibn Niyar stood and said, ‘Messenger of Allah, by Allah, I sacrificed before going out to the prayer. I knew that today was a day of eating and drinking, so I made haste, ate and fed my family and my neighbours.’ The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘That is a sheep for meat.’ He said, ‘I have a young she-goat that is better than two sheep for meat. Will it suffice for me?’ He said, ‘Yes, but it will not suffice for anyone after you.’

I have a young she-goat dearer to me than two sheep for meat.’ He allowed it for him.

english_blocks: Yahya ibn Bukayr related to us. He said: Al-Layth related to us, from ‘Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, from ‘Urwah, from ‘A’ishah:

Abu Bakr, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, came in to her. There were two girls with her during the days of Mina, playing the duff and beating it, while the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was covered with his garment. Abu Bakr rebuked them, so the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, uncovered his face and said, ‘Leave them, Abu Bakr, for these are days of Eid.’
Those days were the days of Mina.

‘A’ishah said: I saw the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, screening me while I watched the Abyssinians playing in the mosque. ‘Umar rebuked them, so the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘Leave them. You are safe, Banu Arfidah.’

english_blocks: ‘Abdullah ibn Maslamah related to us, from Malik, from Makhramah ibn Sulayman, from Kurayb, that Ibn ‘Abbas informed him:

He spent the night with Maymunah, who was his maternal aunt. I lay across the width of a pillow, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and his wife lay along its length. He slept until midnight, or close to it. Then he awoke, wiping sleep from his face, and recited ten verses from Al ‘Imran. Then the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went to an old waterskin that was hanging and performed ablution well. Then he stood to pray. I did as he had done and stood beside him. He placed his right hand on my head and took hold of my ear, twisting it. Then he prayed two units, then two units, then two units, then two units, then two units, then two units. Then he prayed Witr. Then he lay down until the caller to prayer came to him. He got up and prayed two units, then went out and prayed the morning prayer.

arabic_blocks: [962] حدثنا عثمان بن أبي شيبة قال: حدثنا جرير عن منصور عن أبي الضحى عن مسروق قال كنا عند عبد الله، فقال إن النبي ﷺ لما رأى من الناس إدبارا قال اللهم سبع كسبع يوسف فأخذتهم سنة حصت كل شيء حتى أكلوا الجلود والميتة والجيف وينظر أحدهم إلى السماء فيرى الدخان من الجوع فأتاه أبو سفيان، فقال: يا محمد إنك تأمر بطاعة الله وبصلة الرحم وإن قومك قد هلكوا فادع الله لهم قال الله تعالى { فارتقب يوم تأتي السماء بدخان مبين } إلى قوله { عائدون يوم نبطش البطشة الكبرى } فالبطشة يوم بدر وقد مضت الدخان والبطشة واللزام وآية الروم

One of them would look at the sky and see smoke from hunger. Abu Sufyan came to him and said, “O Muhammad, you command obedience to Allah and maintaining ties of kinship. Your people have perished, so supplicate to Allah for them.” Allah Most High said, “So watch for the day when the sky brings clear smoke,” up to His words, “returning—the day We strike the greatest blow.” The blow was on the day of Badr. And a fair one, through whose face rain is sought from the clouds,
a refuge for orphans, a protection for widows.
And ‘Umar ibn Hamzah said: Salim related to us, from his father:
At times I remembered the poet’s words while looking at the face of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, as he sought rain. He would not come down until every waterspout gushed:
And a fair one, through whose face rain is sought from the clouds,
a refuge for orphans, a protection for widows.
And these are Abu Talib’s words.

arabic_blocks: [967] حدثنا محمد قال: أخبرنا أبو ضمرة أنس بن عياض قال: حدثنا شريك بن عبد الله بن أبي نمر أنه سمع أنس بن مالك يذكر أن رجلا دخل يوم الجمعة من باب كان وجاه المنبر ورسول الله ﷺ قائم يخطب فاستقبل رسول الله ﷺ قائما، فقال: يا رسول الله هلكت المواشي وانقطعت السبل فادع الله يغيثنا قال: فرفع رسول الله ﷺ يديه، فقال اللهم اسقنا اللهم اسقنا اللهم اسقنا قال أنس ولا والله ما نرى في السماء من سحاب ولا قزعة ولا شيئا وما بيننا وبين سلع من بيت ولا دار قال: فطلعت من ورائه سحابة مثل الترس فلما توسطت السماء انتشرت ثم أمطرت قال والله ما رأينا الشمس ستا ثم دخل رجل من ذلك الباب في الجمعة المقبلة ورسول الله ﷺ قائم يخطب فاستقبله قائما، فقال: يا رسول الله هلكت الأموال وانقطعت السبل فادع الله يمسكها قال: فرفع رسول الله ﷺ يديه، ثم قال اللهم حوالينا ولا علينا اللهم على الآكام والجبال والآجام والظراب والأودية ومنابت الشجر قال: فانقطعت وخرجنا نمشي في الشمس قال شريك فسألت أنسا أهو الرجل الأول قال لا أدري
english_blocks: Muhammad related to us. He said: Abu Damrah Anas ibn ‘Iyad informed us. He said: Sharik ibn ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Namir related to us that he heard Anas ibn Malik mentioning:

A man entered on Friday through a door facing the pulpit while the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was standing and delivering the sermon. He stood facing the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and said, “O Messenger of Allah, the livestock have perished and the roads have been cut off, so supplicate to Allah to send us rain.” He said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, raised his hands and said, “O Allah, give us rain. O Allah, give us rain. O Allah, give us rain.”

Anas said: No, by Allah, we could see no cloud in the sky, not even a small patch, nor anything at all. There was no house or dwelling between us and Sal‘. He said: A cloud like a shield rose from behind it. When it reached the middle of the sky, it spread out and then rained.

He said: By Allah, we did not see the sun for six days. Then a man entered through that door on the following Friday while the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was standing and delivering the sermon. He stood facing him and said, “O Messenger of Allah, property has been destroyed and the roads have been cut off, so supplicate to Allah to hold it back.” He said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, raised his hands, then said, “O Allah, around us and not upon us. O Allah, upon the high ground, the mountains, the thickets, the low hills, the valleys and the places where trees grow.” He said: It stopped, and we went out walking in the sunshine.
Sharik said: I asked Anas, “Was he the first man?” He said, “I do not know.”

arabic_blocks: [968] حدثنا قتيبة بن سعيد قال: حدثنا إسماعيل بن جعفر عن شريك عن أنس بن مالك أن رجلا دخل المسجد يوم جمعة من باب كان نحو دار القضاء ورسول الله ﷺ قائم يخطب فاستقبل رسول الله ﷺ قائما، ثم قال: يا رسول الله هلكت الأموال وانقطعت السبل فادع الله يغثنا فرفع رسول الله ﷺ يديه، ثم قال اللهم أغثنا اللهم أغثنا اللهم أغثنا قال أنس ولا والله ما نرى في السماء من سحاب ولا قزعة وما بيننا وبين سلع من بيت ولا دار قال: فطلعت من ورائه سحابة مثل الترس فلما توسطت السماء انتشرت ثم أمطرت فلا والله ما رأينا الشمس ستا ثم دخل رجل من ذلك الباب في الجمعة يعني الثانية ورسول الله ﷺ قائم يخطب فاستقبله قائما، فقال: يا رسول الله هلكت الأموال وانقطعت السبل فادع الله يمسكها عنا قال: فرفع رسول الله ﷺ يديه، ثم قال اللهم حوالينا ولا علينا اللهم على الآكام والظراب وبطون الأودية ومنابت الشجر قال: فأقلعت وخرجنا نمشي في الشمس قال شريك سألت أنس بن مالك أهو الرجل الأول، فقال: ما أدري

A man entered the mosque on a Friday through a door towards Dar al-Qada’ while the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was standing and delivering the sermon. He stood facing the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, then said, “O Messenger of Allah, property has been destroyed and the roads have been cut off, so supplicate to Allah to send us rain.” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, raised his hands, then said, “O Allah, come to our aid. O Allah, come to our aid. O Allah, come to our aid.”

Anas said: No, by Allah, we could see no cloud in the sky, not even a small patch. There was no house or dwelling between us and Sal‘. He said: A cloud like a shield rose from behind it. When it reached the middle of the sky, it spread out and then rained. No, by Allah, we did not see the sun for six days.

Then a man entered through that door on Friday—meaning the second Friday—while the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was standing and delivering the sermon. He stood facing him and said, “O Messenger of Allah, property has been destroyed and the roads have been cut off, so supplicate to Allah to hold it back from us.” He said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, raised his hands, then said, “O Allah, around us and not upon us. O Allah, upon the high ground, the low hills, the valley bottoms and the places where trees grow.” He said: It ceased, and we went out walking in the sunshine.

english_blocks: Musaddad related to us. He said: Abu ‘Awanah related to us, from Qatadah, from Anas, who said:

While the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was delivering the sermon on Friday, a man came to him and said, “O Messenger of Allah, the rain has failed, so supplicate to Allah to give us rain.” He supplicated, and rain fell upon us, so that we could hardly reach our homes. Rain continued to fall upon us until the following Friday. He said: That man, or someone else, stood up and said, “O Messenger of Allah, supplicate to Allah to turn it away from us.” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “O Allah, around us and not upon us.” He said: I saw the clouds breaking apart to the right and the left. They received rain, but the people of Medina did not.

arabic_blocks: [971] حدثنا إسماعيل قال: حدثني مالك عن شريك بن عبد الله بن أبي نمر عن أنس بن مالك قال جاء رجل إلى رسول الله ﷺ، فقال: يا رسول الله هلكت المواشي وانقطعت السبل فادع الله فدعا رسول الله ﷺ فمطروا من جمعة إلى جمعة فجاء رجل إلى رسول الله ﷺ، فقال: يا رسول الله تهدمت البيوت وتقطعت السبل وهلكت المواشي، فقال رسول الله ﷺ: اللهم على رؤوس الجبال والآكام وبطون الأودية ومنابت الشجر فانجابت عن المدينة انجياب الثوب
english_blocks: Isma‘il related to us. He said: Malik related to me, from Sharik ibn ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Namir, from Anas ibn Malik, who said:

A man came to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and said, “O Messenger of Allah, the houses have collapsed, the roads have been cut off and the livestock have perished.” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “O Allah, upon the mountaintops, the high ground, the valley bottoms and the places where trees grow.” It cleared away from Medina as a garment is drawn off.

arabic_blocks: [974] حدثنا محمد بن كثير عن سفيان حدثنا منصور والأعمش عن أبي الضحى عن مسروق قال أتيت بن مسعود، فقال إن قريشا أبطؤوا عن الإسلام فدعا عليهم النبي ﷺ فأخذتهم سنة حتى هلكوا فيها وأكلوا الميتة والعظام فجاءه أبو سفيان، فقال: يا محمد جئت تأمر بصلة الرحم وإن قومك هلكوا فادع الله فقرأ { فارتقب يوم تأتي السماء بدخان مبين } ثم عادوا إلى كفرهم فذلك قوله تعالى { يوم نبطش البطشة الكبرى } يوم بدر قال أبو عبد الله وزاد أسباط عن منصور فدعا رسول الله ﷺ فسقوا الغيث فأطبقت عليهم سبعا وشكا الناس كثرة المطر قال اللهم حوالينا ولا علينا فانحدرت السحابة عن رأسه فسقوا الناس حولهم
english_blocks: Muhammad ibn Kathir related to us, from Sufyan: Mansur and al-A‘mash related to us, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, who said:

I went to Ibn Mas‘ud, and he said: Quraysh were slow to accept Islam, so the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, supplicated against them. A year of scarcity overtook them, until they were perishing in it and ate carrion and bones. Abu Sufyan came to him and said, “O Muhammad, you came commanding that ties of kinship be maintained, and your people have perished, so supplicate to Allah.” He recited, “So watch for the day when the sky brings clear smoke.” Then they returned to their disbelief. That is His saying, Most High, “The day We strike the greatest blow”—the day of Badr.
Abu ‘Abdullah said: Asbat added, from Mansur:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, supplicated, and they were given rain. It covered them for seven days, and the people complained of the abundance of rain. He said, “O Allah, around us and not upon us.” The cloud moved down from above his head, and the people around them were given rain.

arabic_blocks: [975] حدثنا محمد بن أبي بكر حدثنا معتمر عن عبيد الله عن ثابت عن أنس قال: كان النبي ﷺ يخطب يوم جمعة فقام الناس فصاحوا فقالوا يا رسول الله قحط المطر واحمرت الشجر وهلكت البهائم فادع الله أن يسقينا، فقال اللهم اسقنا مرتين وأيم الله ما نرى في السماء قزعة من سحاب فنشأت سحابة وأمطرت ونزل عن المنبر فصلى فلما انصرف لم تزل تمطر إلى الجمعة التي تليها فلما قام النبي ﷺ يخطب صاحوا إليه تهدمت البيوت وانقطعت السبل فادع الله يحبسها عنا فتبسم النبي ﷺ، ثم قال اللهم حوالينا ولا علينا فكشطت المدينة فجعلت تمطر حولها ولا تمطر بالمدينة قطرة فنظرت إلى المدينة وإنها لفي مثل الإكليل
english_blocks: Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr related to us. Mu‘tamir related to us, from ‘Ubaydullah, from Thabit, from Anas, who said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was delivering the sermon on a Friday. The people stood up and cried out, saying, “O Messenger of Allah, the rain has failed, the trees have reddened and the animals have perished, so supplicate to Allah to give us rain.” He said, “O Allah, give us rain,” twice. By Allah, we could see no patch of cloud in the sky. A cloud formed and rained. He came down from the pulpit and prayed. When he had finished, it continued raining until the following Friday.

When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood to deliver the sermon, they cried out to him, “The houses have collapsed and the roads have been cut off, so supplicate to Allah to hold it back from us.” The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, smiled, then said, “O Allah, around us and not upon us.” It cleared away from Medina and began raining around it, while not a drop fell in Medina. I looked at Medina, and it was as though it were within a wreath.

arabic_blocks: [983] قال أيوب بن سليمان حدثني أبو بكر ابن أبي أويس عن سليمان بن بلال قال يحيى بن سعيد سمعت أنس بن مالك قال أتى رجل أعرابي من أهل البدو إلى رسول الله ﷺ يوم الجمعة، فقال: يا رسول الله هلكت الماشية هلك العيال هلك الناس فرفع رسول الله ﷺ يديه يدعو ورفع الناس أيديهم معه يدعون قال: فما خرجنا من المسجد حتى مطرنا فما زلنا نمطر حتى كانت الجمعة الأخرى فأتى الرجل إلى نبي الله ﷺ، فقال: يا رسول الله بشق المسافر ومنع الطريق
english_blocks: Ayyub ibn Sulayman said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Uways related to me, from Sulayman ibn Bilal. Yahya ibn Sa‘id said: I heard Anas ibn Malik say:

A Bedouin man from the desert people came to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, on Friday and said, “O Messenger of Allah, the livestock have perished, the dependants have perished, the people have perished.” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, raised his hands, supplicating, and the people raised their hands with him, supplicating.

He said: We had not left the mosque before rain fell upon us. Rain continued to fall upon us until the following Friday. The man came to the Prophet of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and said, “O Messenger of Allah, the traveller is unable to proceed and the road is blocked.”

The people were afflicted by a year of drought during the time of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. While the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was delivering the sermon on the pulpit on Friday, a Bedouin stood up and said, “O Messenger of Allah, the property has perished and the dependants have gone hungry. Supplicate to Allah for us to give us rain.”

He said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, raised his hands, and there was not a small cloud in the sky. He said: Clouds like mountains rose up. He had not yet descended from his pulpit when I saw rain streaming down his beard.

He said: Rain fell upon us that day, the next day, the day after that and the following day, until the next Friday. That Bedouin, or another man, stood up and said, “O Messenger of Allah, the buildings have collapsed and the property has been submerged. Supplicate to Allah for us.” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, raised his hands and said, “O Allah, around us and not upon us.”

He said: Whenever he pointed with his hand towards a part of the sky, it cleared, until Madinah was like an open space. The valley—the valley of Qanat—flowed for a month. He said: No one came from any direction without speaking of the abundant rain.

english_blocks: ‘Abdullah ibn Maslamah related to us, from Malik, from Hisham ibn ‘Urwah, from his father, from ‘Aishah, who said:

The sun was eclipsed in the time of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, led the people in prayer. He stood and prolonged the standing, then bowed and prolonged the bowing. Then he stood and prolonged the standing, but it was shorter than the first standing. Then he bowed and prolonged the bowing, but it was shorter than the first bowing. Then he prostrated and prolonged the prostration. Then he did in the second rak‘ah as he had done in the first. Then he finished, and the sun had cleared. He addressed the people, praised Allah and extolled Him.

Then he said: “The sun and the moon are two of Allah’s signs. They are not eclipsed because of anyone’s death or life. When you see this, supplicate to Allah, proclaim His greatness, pray and give charity.”

Then he said: “O community of Muhammad, by Allah, no one has greater ghayrah than Allah concerning His male servant committing unlawful sexual intercourse or His female servant committing unlawful sexual intercourse. O community of Muhammad, by Allah, if you knew what I know, you would laugh little and weep much.”

arabic_blocks: [999] حدثنا يحيى بن بكير قال: حدثني الليث عن عقيل عن ابن شهاب ح وحدثني أحمد بن صالح قال: حدثنا عنبسة قال: حدثنا يونس عن ابن شهاب حدثني عروة عن عائشة زوج النبي ﷺ قالت خسفت الشمس في حياة النبي ﷺ فخرج إلى المسجد فصف الناس وراءه فكبر فاقترأ رسول الله ﷺ قراءة طويلة ثم كبر فركع ركوعا طويلا، ثم قال سمع الله لمن حمده فقام ولم يسجد وقرأ قراءة طويلة هي أدنى من القراءة الأولى ثم كبر وركع ركوعا طويلا وهو أدنى من الركوع الأول، ثم قال سمع الله لمن حمده ربنا ولك الحمد ثم سجد، ثم قال في الركعة الآخرة مثل ذلك فاستكمل أربع ركعات في أربع سجدات وانجلت الشمس قبل أن ينصرف ثم قام فأثنى على الله بما هو أهله، ثم قال هما آيتان من آيات الله لا يخسفان لموت أحد ولا لحياته فإذا رأيتموهما فافزعوا إلى الصلاة وكان يحدث كثير بن عباس أن عبد الله بن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما كان يحدث يوم خسفت الشمس بمثل حديث عروة عن عائشة فقلت لعروة إن أخاك يوم خسفت بالمدينة لم يزد على ركعتين مثل الصبح قال أجل لأنه أخطأ السنة
english_blocks: Yahya ibn Bukayr related to us. He said: al-Layth related to me, from ‘Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab.

Another chain: Ahmad ibn Salih related to me. He said: ‘Anbasah related to us. He said: Yunus related to us, from Ibn Shihab: ‘Urwah related to me, from ‘Aishah, the wife of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

The sun was eclipsed during the life of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He went out to the mosque, and the people formed rows behind him. He proclaimed Allah’s greatness, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, recited at length. Then he proclaimed Allah’s greatness and bowed for a long time. Then he said: “Allah hears whoever praises Him.” He stood and did not prostrate, and recited at length, but less than the first recitation. Then he proclaimed Allah’s greatness and bowed for a long time, but less than the first bowing. Then he said: “Allah hears whoever praises Him. Our Lord, to You belongs praise.” Then he prostrated. Then he said the like of that in the other rak‘ah, completing four bowings in four prostrations. The sun cleared before he finished.
Then he stood and praised Allah as He deserves. Then he said: “They are two of Allah’s signs. They are not eclipsed because of anyone’s death or life. When you see them, hasten to prayer.”

Kathir ibn ‘Abbas used to relate that ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, used to relate an account of the day the sun was eclipsed like ‘Urwah’s report from ‘Aishah. I said to ‘Urwah: “On the day it was eclipsed in Madinah, your brother did not pray more than two rak‘ahs, like the dawn prayer.” He said: “Yes, because he was mistaken about the Sunnah.”

english_blocks: ‘Abdullah ibn Maslamah related to us, from Malik, from Yahya ibn Sa‘id, from ‘Amrah bint ‘Abd al-Rahman, from ‘Aishah, the wife of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

A Jewish woman came to ask her, and said to her: “May Allah protect you from the punishment of the grave.” ‘Aishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, asked the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: “Are people punished in their graves?” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “I seek refuge in Allah from that.”

Then one morning the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went riding, and the sun was eclipsed. He returned in the forenoon. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, passed among the chambers. Then he stood to pray, and the people stood behind him.

He stood for a long time, then bowed for a long time. Then he rose and stood for a long time, but less than the first standing. Then he bowed for a long time, but less than the first bowing. Then he rose and prostrated. Then he stood, and stood for a long time, but less than the first standing. Then he bowed for a long time, but less than the first bowing. Then he stood for a long time, but less than the first standing. Then he bowed for a long time, but less than the first bowing. Then he rose and prostrated. He finished and said what Allah willed him to say. Then he instructed them to seek refuge from the punishment of the grave.

arabic_blocks: [1004] حدثنا عبد الله بن مسلمة عن مالك عن زيد بن أسلم عن عطاء بن يسار عن عبد الله بن عباس قال انخسفت الشمس على عهد رسول الله ﷺ فصلى رسول الله ﷺ فقام قياما طويلا نحوا من قراءة سورة البقرة ثم ركع ركوعا طويلا ثم رفع فقام قياما طويلا وهو دون القيام الأول ثم ركع ركوعا طويلا وهو دون الركوع الأول ثم سجد ثم قام قياما طويلا وهو دون القيام الأول ثم ركع ركوعا طويلا وهو دون الركوع الأول ثم رفع فقام قياما طويلا وهو دون القيام الأول ثم ركع ركوعا طويلا وهو دون الركوع الأول ثم سجد ثم انصرف وقد تجلت الشمس، فقال ﷺ إن الشمس والقمر آيتان من آيات الله لا يخسفان لموت أحد ولا لحياته فإذا رأيتم ذلك فاذكروا الله قالوا يا رسول الله رأيناك تناولت شيئا في مقامك ثم رأيناك كعكعت قال ﷺ إني رأيت الجنة فتناولت عنقودا ولو أصبته لأكلتم منه ما بقيت الدنيا وأريت النار فلم أر منظرا كاليوم قط أفظع ورأيت أكثر أهلها النساء قالوا بم يا رسول الله قال بكفرهن قيل يكفرن بالله قال يكفرن العشير ويكفرن الإحسان لو أحسنت إلى إحداهن الدهر كله ثم رأت منك شيئا قالت ما رأيت منك خيرا قط
english_blocks: ‘Abdullah ibn Maslamah related to us, from Malik, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from ‘Ata’ ibn Yasar, from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas, who said:

The sun was eclipsed in the time of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed. He stood for a long time, about as long as the recitation of Surat al-Baqarah. Then he bowed for a long time. Then he rose and stood for a long time, but less than the first standing. Then he bowed for a long time, but less than the first bowing. Then he prostrated. Then he stood for a long time, but less than the first standing. Then he bowed for a long time, but less than the first bowing. Then he rose and stood for a long time, but less than the first standing. Then he bowed for a long time, but less than the first bowing. Then he prostrated. Then he finished, and the sun had cleared.
Then he, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “The sun and the moon are two of Allah’s signs. They are not eclipsed because of anyone’s death or life. When you see that, remember Allah.”

They said: “Messenger of Allah, we saw you reach for something where you stood, then we saw you draw back.” He, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “I saw Paradise and reached for a cluster. Had I taken it, you would have eaten from it for as long as the world remains. I was shown the Fire, and I have never seen a sight more dreadful than today’s. I saw that most of its inhabitants were women.”

They said: “Why, Messenger of Allah?” He said: “Because of their ingratitude.” It was said: “Do they disbelieve in Allah?” He said: “They are ungrateful to their husbands and ungrateful for kindness. If you were kind to one of them for all time, then she saw something from you, she would say: ‘I have never seen any good from you.’”

english_blocks: ‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Hisham ibn ‘Urwah, from his wife Fatimah bint al-Mundhir, from Asma’ bint Abi Bakr, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, who said:

I came to ‘Aishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, the wife of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, when the sun was eclipsed. The people were standing in prayer, and she was standing in prayer. I said: “What is happening with the people?” She pointed with her hand toward the sky and said: “Glory be to Allah.” I said: “A sign?” She indicated: yes. She said: I stood until faintness overcame me, and I began pouring water over my head. When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, finished, he praised Allah and extolled Him.

Then he said: “There is nothing I had not seen before but that I have seen it while standing here, even Paradise and the Fire. It has been revealed to me that you will be tested in the graves with a trial like, or close to, the trial of the Dajjal—
I do not know which of the two Asma’ said.
one of you will be approached and asked: ‘What do you know of this man?’ As for the believer, or the one who is certain—
I do not know which of those Asma’ said.

he will say: ‘Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came to us with clear proofs and guidance. We responded, believed and followed.’ It will be said to him: ‘Sleep in peace; we have known that you were indeed certain.’ As for the hypocrite, or the one who doubts—
I do not know which of the two Asma’ said.
he will say: ‘I do not know. I heard people saying something, so I said it.’”

A Jewish woman came to ask her, and said: “May Allah protect you from the punishment of the grave.” ‘Aishah asked the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: “Are people punished in their graves?” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “I seek refuge in Allah from that.”

Then one morning the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went riding, and the sun was eclipsed. He returned in the forenoon. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, passed among the chambers. Then he stood and prayed, and the people stood behind him.

He stood for a long time, then bowed for a long time. Then he rose and stood for a long time, but less than the first standing. Then he bowed for a long time, but less than the first bowing. Then he rose and prostrated for a long time. Then he stood, and stood for a long time, but less than the first standing. Then he bowed for a long time, but less than the first bowing. Then he stood for a long time, but less than the first standing. Then he bowed for a long time, but less than the first bowing. Then he prostrated, but less than the first prostration.
Then he finished, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said what Allah willed him to say. Then he instructed them to seek refuge from the punishment of the grave.

He said: “The sun and the moon are two of Allah’s signs. They are not eclipsed because of anyone’s death. When that happens, pray and supplicate until what has come upon you is removed.”
That was because a son of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had died, called Ibrahim, and the people spoke about that.

arabic_blocks: [1016] حدثنا محمد بن مهران قال: حدثنا الوليد قال: أخبرنا ابن نمر سمع ابن شهاب عن عروة عن عائشة رضى الله تعالى عنها جهر النبي ﷺ في صلاة الخسوف بقراءته فإذا فرغ من قراءته كبر فركع وإذا رفع من الركعة قال سمع الله لمن حمده ربنا ولك الحمد ثم يعاود القراءة في صلاة الكسوف أربع ركعات في ركعتين وأربع سجدات، وقال الأوزاعي وغيره سمعت الزهري عن عروة عن عائشة رضى الله تعالى عنها أن الشمس خسفت على عهد رسول الله ﷺ فبعث مناديا ب الصلاة جامعة فتقدم فصلى أربع ركعات في ركعتين وأربع سجدات وأخبرني عبد الرحمن بن نمر سمع ابن شهاب مثله قال الزهري فقلت: ما صنع أخوك ذلك عبد الله بن الزبير ما صلى إلا ركعتين مثل الصبح إذ صلى بالمدينة قال أجل إنه أخطأ السنة تابعه سفيان بن حسين وسليمان بن كثير عن الزهري في الجهر
english_blocks: Muhammad ibn Mihran related to us. He said: al-Walid related to us. He said: Ibn Namir informed us; he heard Ibn Shihab, from ‘Urwah, from ‘Aishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, recited aloud in the eclipse prayer. When he finished his recitation, he proclaimed Allah’s greatness and bowed. When he rose from the bowing, he said: “Allah hears whoever praises Him. Our Lord, and to You belongs praise.” Then he resumed recitation. In the eclipse prayer there were four bowings in two rak‘ahs and four prostrations.
Al-Awza‘i and others said: I heard al-Zuhri, from ‘Urwah, from ‘Aishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, that:

The sun was eclipsed during the time of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He sent a caller to announce: “Prayer in congregation.” Then he went forward and prayed four bowings in two rak‘ahs and four prostrations.
And ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Namir informed me that he heard the same from Ibn Shihab.

Al-Zuhri said: I said: “Your brother, ‘Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, did not do that. He prayed only two rak‘ahs, like the dawn prayer, when he prayed in Madinah.” He said: “Yes, he was mistaken about the Sunnah.”
Sufyan ibn Husayn and Sulayman ibn Kathir followed him in transmitting from al-Zuhri about reciting aloud.

english_blocks: Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Salim informed me, from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, who said:

I saw the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, when travelling in haste on a journey, delay Maghrib until he combined it with ‘Isha’. Salim said: ‘Abdullah used to do this when travelling in haste.
Al-Layth added. He said: Yunus related to me, from Ibn Shihab. Salim said:
Ibn ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, used to combine Maghrib and ‘Isha’ at Muzdalifah.

Salim said: Ibn ‘Umar delayed Maghrib when he had been urgently called to help concerning his wife, Safiyyah bint Abi ‘Ubayd. I said to him, “The prayer!” He said, “Go on.” I said, “The prayer!” He said, “Go on,” until he had travelled two or three miles. Then he dismounted and prayed. Then he said, “This is how I saw the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, pray when travelling in haste.”

‘Abdullah said: I saw the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, when travelling in haste, delay Maghrib and pray it as three rak‘ahs, then say the taslim. Then he would wait only a little before saying the iqamah for ‘Isha’, praying it as two rak‘ahs, and saying the taslim. He would not pray voluntary prayers after ‘Isha’ until he rose during the middle of the night.

arabic_blocks: [1058] حدثنا أبو اليمان قال: أخبرنا شعيب عن الزهري قال: أخبرني سالم عن عبد الله بن عمر رضى الله تعالى عنهما قال: رأيت رسول الله ﷺ إذا أعجله السير في السفر يؤخر صلاة المغرب حتى يجمع بينها وبين العشاء قال سالم وكان عبد الله يفعله إذا أعجله السير ويقيم المغرب فيصليها ثلاثا ثم يسلم ثم قلما يلبث حتى يقيم العشاء فيصليها ركعتين ثم يسلم ولا يسبح بينهما بركعة ولا بعد العشاء بسجدة حتى يقوم من جوف الليل
english_blocks: Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Salim informed me, from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, who said:
I saw the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, when travelling in haste on a journey, delay the Maghrib prayer until he combined it with ‘Isha’.

Salim said: ‘Abdullah used to do this when travelling in haste. He would say the iqamah for Maghrib and pray it as three rak‘ahs, then say the taslim. Then he would wait only a little before saying the iqamah for ‘Isha’, praying it as two rak‘ahs, then saying the taslim. He would not pray a single voluntary rak‘ah between them, nor a prostration after ‘Isha’, until he rose during the middle of the night.

english_blocks: ‘Ali ibn ‘Abdullah related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us. He said: Sulayman ibn Abi Muslim related to us, from Tawus, who heard Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, say:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, when he rose during the night for tahajjud, would say: “O Allah, to You belongs praise. You are the Sustainer of the heavens and the earth and those within them. To You belongs praise. Yours is the dominion of the heavens and the earth and those within them. To You belongs praise. You are the Light of the heavens and the earth and those within them. To You belongs praise. You are the King of the heavens and the earth. To You belongs praise. You are the Truth. Your promise is the truth; meeting You is true; Your word is true; Paradise is true; the Fire is true; the prophets are true; Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, is true; and the Hour is true. O Allah, to You I have submitted, in You I have believed, on You I have relied, and to You I have turned. By You I have argued, and to You I have brought my case for judgment. Forgive me what I have done earlier and later, what I have concealed and what I have made public. You are the One who brings forward and the One who puts back. There is no god except You,” or, “There is no god other than You.”
Sufyan said: ‘Abd al-Karim Abu Umayyah added, “And there is no power and no strength except through Allah.”
Sufyan said: Sulayman ibn Abi Muslim said that he heard it from Tawus, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

english_blocks: ‘Abdullah ibn Muhammad related to us. He said: Hisham related to us. He said: Ma‘mar informed us. And Mahmud related to me. He said: ‘Abd al-Razzaq related to us. He said: Ma‘mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Salim, from his father, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, who said:

During the lifetime of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, when a man saw a dream, he would recount it to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. I wished to see a dream so that I could recount it to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. I was a young man, and I used to sleep in the mosque during the time of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. In my sleep I saw as though two angels took me and brought me to the Fire. It was built around like the lining of a well, and it had two uprights. There were people in it whom I recognized. I began saying, “I seek refuge in Allah from the Fire.” He said: Then another angel met us and said to me, “You need not be afraid.”

I recounted it to Hafsah, and Hafsah recounted it to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He said, “What a fine man ‘Abdullah is! If only he prayed during the night.” After that, he slept only a little during the night.

arabic_blocks: [1077] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: أخبرنا مالك عن ابن شهاب عن عروة بن الزبير عن عائشة أم المؤمنين رضى الله تعالى عنها أن رسول الله ﷺ صلى ذات ليلة في المسجد فصلى بصلاته ناس ثم صلى من القابلة فكثر الناس ثم اجتمعوا من الليلة الثالثة أو الرابعة فلم يخرج إليهم رسول الله ﷺ فلما أصبح قال قد رأيت الذي صنعتم ولم يمنعني من الخروج إليكم إلا أني خشيت أن تفرض عليكم وذلك في رمضان
english_blocks: ‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Ibn Shihab, from ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, from ‘A’ishah, the Mother of the Believers, may Allah Most High be pleased with her:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed one night in the mosque, and some people followed his prayer. Then he prayed on the following night, and the people grew in number. Then they gathered on the third or fourth night, but the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, did not come out to them. When morning came, he said, “I saw what you did. Nothing prevented me from coming out to you except my fear that it would be made obligatory for you.” That was in Ramadan.
